messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — production: inference error rate spike detected for model orca-v2-1b in us-west-2. Errors > 20% for 5m. Paging on-call.

maya: acked, oncall here. seeing the alert. pulling metrics and recent deploys.

sam: thanks maya. can you confirm customer impact? ops dashboard shows a few 5xxs and some timeouts.

maya: quick look: 5xxs ~24% of requests to /v1/generate for orca-v2-1b, latency also up from 120ms -> 900ms p95. top customers by volume: acme-inc, quickchat.

lee: joining — I was on the model rollout earlier. We started a canary at 2026-03-14T06:12:30Z deploying orca-v2-1b+tokenizer-update. Canary size 2% traffic.

ana: (typo) ana: I mean thanks — I'm pulling logs from runtime.

maya: paste logs below, trimmed.

```
2026-03-14T06:14:02Z runtime[worker-23]: ERR tokenization_failed: invalid byte sequence
2026-03-14T06:14:03Z runtime[worker-23]: WARN kv_cache: eviction spike, used=98% total=32GB
2026-03-14T06:14:03Z runtime[worker-24]: ERR decoder: cuda out of memory when allocating 128MB
2026-03-14T06:14:04Z runtime[router]: WARN model-mismatch: requested orca-v2-1b, served orca-v2-1b+tokenizer-update
```

maya: interesting — tokenization errors + OOMs around same time. maybe tokenizer change produced longer token sequences?

sam: or the newer tokenizer changed byte handling making some inputs produce invalid sequences. any repro?

lee: I ran a local replay of failing request — observed tokenization exception when input includes emojis + certain unicode combining chars. tokenizer update changed fallback handling.

ana: ana here — also seeing a KB of tracebacks indicating a mismatch between model build and runtime tokenizer lib version. Could be packaging mishap in the canary image.

maya: customer impact: estimate ~1.2k requests failed in 15m window, ~0.04% of total global traffic but concentrated in a handful of customers in us-west-2 region. severity: P1 impact to affected customers; global service still up.

jess: looping in product: have we sent any comms to affected customers yet?

sam: not yet — wait for mitigation plan.

maya: mitigation options: 1) disable canary routing to that model variant (stop sending new canary traffic), 2) rollback canary by pinning traffic back to orca-v2-1a, 3) hotfix tokenizer lib and redeploy.

lee: hotfix might take 30–60m to build + test. disabling canary routing is immediate. rollback gives full safety but will affect canary testing.

ana: recommend immediate rollback/pinning for the canary group. stop further canary traffic and abort ongoing canary requests.

maya: executing rollback pin now. pinging deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: command received: `redwood deploy rollback --env=production --model=orca-v2-1b+tokenizer-update --to=orca-v2-1a --scope=canary`

deploy-bot: rollback started; expected completion 30s–2m.

maya: rollback completed on router. verified: canary traffic back to orca-v2-1a. monitoring metrics...

(30s later)

maya: errors dropped to baseline, p95 latency back to ~130ms. 5xxs gone.

sam: nice. confirm we didn't affect Dedicated/reserved pools?

lee: checked isolated pools — dedicated pools in other regions unaffected. issue confined to canary routing group in us-west-2.

ana: hypothesis tracking:
- Hypothesis A: tokenizer packaging mismatch in canary image -> tokenization_failed exceptions (supported by tracebacks).
- Hypothesis B: tokenizer change leads to longer sequences causing KV cache pressure -> OOMs (plausible; metrics show KV cache jump).
- Hypothesis C: unrelated runtime kernel change coincidentally triggered OOMs (less likely; no kernel deploys at same time).

maya: tagging Hypothesis A high-confidence; B medium; C low.

jess: next steps / action items:
- (jess) notify affected customers with incident summary and apology — include rollback info and ETA for fix.
- (lee) reproduce locally & build hotfix for tokenizer packaging; validate against unicode fuzz corpus.
- (ana) collect full traces, logs (router + worker), and upload to incident bucket.
- (maya) follow up with oncall doc + add to timeline.

sam: also add a gating check to canary pipeline: validate tokenizer version parity between model bundle and runtime container. If mismatch, fail canary rollout.

lee: I'll add an integration test and a preflight that compares tokenizer git SHA in build metadata vs runtime lib at startup.

maya: quick evidence summary for RCA:
- timeline: 06:12:30Z canary started -> 06:14Z tokenization errors & OOMs -> 06:15:10Z paging triggered -> 06:18Z rollback initiated -> 06:18:40Z rollback complete -> 06:19:10Z errors resolved.
- impacted: ~1.2k failed requests, top customers: acme-inc (420 fails), quickchat (210 fails).
- root cause (initial): mismatched tokenizer packaging in canary image leading to tokenization exceptions; secondary effect: cache pressure & transient OOM on workers.

ana: I'll attach raw logs to the incident ticket and mark for further collection: worker-23 core dump (if exists), router traces, deployment artifact IDs.

jess: leaving notes for communications: recommend targeted email + status page update. hold on public slack post until customer comms sent.

maya: handoff: I'm pausing oncall now — ana will continue follow-ups. ana, you have the incident.

ana: ack. taking ownership for RCA and follow-up tasks. I'll file RCA draft in /incidents/2026/1822501234-rca.md and ping the release lead.

sam: also add an immediate CI gate to prevent tokenizer metadata downgrades.

deploy-bot: activity log: `2026-03-14T06:18:07Z rollback executed by maya (oncall)`

maya: thanks team. closing thread for now — will re-open if anomalies reappear. :white_check_mark:
